title: Dutch students walk out across cities against military conscription

tea.why: Students are protesting against military conscription and increased defense spending at the expense of education, care, and housing.
tea.want: Protesters demand an end to military conscription, the removal of the defense ministry from schools, and investments in youth futures.
tea.changed: Nov 20: Students planned nationwide classroom walkouts at 1pm across at least 16 Dutch cities as part of an international action day.

summary: High school and university students across at least 16 Dutch cities announced a classroom walkout at 1:00 p.m. as part of an international protest day spanning countries like Germany, France, and England. Organised by groups including Stop the War Fever and the National Student Union (LSVb), the action objects to rising defense budgets, recruitment campaigns in schools, and preparations for a selective military conscription system. Participants plan to gather at locations such as the Stopera in Amsterdam and Domplein in Utrecht. Organisers stated that funding is being diverted from housing, healthcare, and education toward weapons and war. Junior minister Derk Boswijk previously noted in March that the deployment of young people could not be ruled out in coming years.
demands: No Ministry of Defense presence at schools
Investment in the future of young people rather than weaponry
response: Junior minister Derk Boswijk stated in March that he could not rule out the deployment of young people in the coming years due to security reasons. No immediate official response to the walkout was reported in the sources.

updates.text: Students across at least 16 Dutch cities scheduled classroom walkouts at 1pm to protest conscription and defense spending.
